acceptance_condition: A structured extraction covering both files with at least 8 findings total, each with file path + PDF page marker, including Lorenz's diversity/accuracy effects under each information condition and Choi's conformity measures and moderators.
rationale: These two papers supply the social-influence/conformity pathway of the causal model (D3): the mechanism by which open transcripts destroy the error independence that makes aggregation work, which is central to why staged retrieval-mediated Q/A might beat an open transcript.
text: Extract from papers/text/lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt and papers/text/choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt: (a) Lorenz et al.'s experimental design and quantitative findings on how social influence (full vs. aggregated information feedback) affects estimate diversity, collective accuracy, and confidence in human crowds; (b) Choi et al.'s findings on group conformity in LLM multi-agent systems — when agents conform, what drives conformity (e.g., majority pressure, model identity, task), and measured effects on accuracy; (c) any parameters or effect sizes usable as priors for modeling error-correlation collapse under shared information. Record each finding with file path and explicit `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
